checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in MS
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: Licensed plumbing/gas contractor pulls the permit on the homeowner's behalf — their license number must appear on the application. Mississippi does not have statewide contractor licensing, so Jackson/local requirements should be verified before filing. Owner-builder status does not remove the permit requirement for gas piping work.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to City of Jackson Office of Code Services

common_mistakes: Starting the gas line work before the permit is issued and posted — the city can stop the job and require corrections before inspection
Using the wrong permit type — this is gas piping work, so it should not be filed as a building permit
Burying or concealing the gas line before the rough-in/pressure test inspection is approved
Not providing the actual project valuation — Jackson uses valuation-based fees, so underreporting the job value can delay approval
